answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a biometric relic: a fingerprint card pressed in pigment at a licensed enrollment center, witnessed in person. Fingerprints cannot be bought or cloned, so one relic belongs to exactly one human. Later, unpredictable echo checks require the same registered finger to scan live within minutes, and no one can staff many seats at once. The enrollment fee in outside money doubles per relic on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real body, another in-person visit, and twice the prior fee; duplicate prints flag the cluster.
